Past work: New Image

How my New Image work was done, in three diagrams.

The real work belongs to New Image's clients, so I rebuilt it as diagrams.

Email newsletters

Every newsletter waits for approval before it goes out.

A brief becomes an email, is checked against the brand rules, and goes out only once someone approves it. I built 38 and 31 went out.

Overview

One newsletter

A brief becomes an email and is checked before it goes out. Tap a step to see it.

  1. Write the brief Each email newsletter starts as one brief and one set of content.
  2. Build the email The email is built from one template with one text file per language: English, Chinese and Bahasa Malaysia.
  3. Brand check The draft is checked against the brand rules before it is uploaded to Moosend.
  4. Approval Every draft waits for approval before it goes out.
Countries

The right pack in every country

One post becomes one image per country, showing that country's product pack and language.

Needs a native speaker

Overview

16 countries

A table picks the language and the official product pack for each country. Tap the post, a country or the total.

  1. One post The post is built once.
  2. Sixteen countries The tool holds each country's language and official product pack. A country that needs a line from a native speaker is marked.
  3. The total 16 countries, each with its own language and product pack.
Build and review

Built by a program, checked on a review page

Posts are built from a list, then sent to a review page where all the notes come back in one place.

Review page
Checked again

Overview

Four steps

Posts are built from a list and sent to a review page. Tap a step to see what happens there.

  1. The program builds posts A program builds posts, carousels and reels from a list of the posts to make, so I do not build each by hand.
  2. The team checks them The team checks each post on phone or desktop and leaves notes.
  3. Notes go back together The notes come back together, and the posts are fixed.
  4. Approved posts Approved posts are ready to publish.

How I work

Plan, build, check, send.

How I would run a webinar for you: four steps, repeated for every one.

  1. Plan

    One run sheet counted from the start time, so the host, the speaker and the coordinator share one sheet. Date, time and time zone are written once and reused everywhere.

  2. Build

    The registration page, invite, reminders and follow-ups from one template and one text file per version, so nothing is rebuilt by hand.

  3. Check

    Every draft goes on a review page. A person approves it, notes come back together, and the join link is tested on a phone and a laptop.

  4. Send

    Send on schedule, then fill in the numbers sheet: registered, attended, clicked, booked. That sheet plans the next webinar.
